source.title: Content Requirements for Survey Plans and Sketches for Dispositions on Crown Lands

clauses.summary: Prepare an original computer-drafted plan with accurate scale, readable organization, and clear uncluttered presentation.

questions: Is this the original plan prepared for the proposed activity, with its origin and revision identity established rather than an unexplained reproduction?
Is the plan legible at its intended plotted size? Inspect the source drawing rather than relying on extracted text presence.
Is the arrangement of plan information well organized so that the proposed activity and its evidence can be followed?
Is the presentation uncluttered, with overlapping information resolved sufficiently for independent review?
Is the source plan computer drafted? Record the supplied source/version evidence and unresolved origin questions.
Is the drawing accurately drawn to its stated scale? Compare the plotted representation with independently accepted dimensions without treating a printed ratio as proof.

clauses.summary: Make the proposed activity and its intended purpose clear on the plan.

questions: Does the plan clearly convey the intent of the proposed activity for this application? Compare its extents and purpose with the authoritative application evidence.

clauses.summary: Keep the sheet between letter size and the stated maximum dimensions.

questions: Is sheet width no more than75cm, or is an applicable regulator-granted exception documented? Inspect physical plotting dimensions and the exact exception scope.
Is sheet length no more than300cm, or is an applicable regulator-granted exception documented? Do not infer an exception from a long activity alone.
Is the sheet at least letter size? Record the intended sheet/plot settings and resolve ambiguous orientation or size evidence.

clauses.summary: Use a listed main-plan scale unless a documented exception applies.

questions: Does the main plan use1:500,1:1000,1:2000,1:2500,1:5000 or1:10000, unless a specific applicable manual provision or documented regulator exception permits another scale? Identify that provision/exception before accepting an alternative.

For the established congested-area details, was the permission to use any scale or not-to-scale adopted? Review their labeling and source context; this permission does not create a mandatory detail or waive main-plan requirements.

clauses.summary: Limit multi-sheet plans to the permitted disposition context.

questions: Does the sheet-count arrangement comply with the source limitation of multipage plans to MSLs, unless a specific Part4 exception applies? Establish actual page count and the exact applicable exception; a long route or several polygons alone is not permission.

clauses.summary: Keep separate linear segments off a shared plan unless an exception applies.

questions: Are multiple non-contiguous linear segments kept off one plan unless a regulator-granted exception or exact applicable Part4 provision permits this presentation? Review written approval/source conditions; tie requirements alone do not authorize non-contiguity.

clauses.summary: Keep separate non-linear activities off a shared plan unless an exception applies.

questions: Are multiple non-contiguous non-linear activities, with or without access, kept off one plan unless a regulator-granted exception or exact applicable Part4 provision permits them? Record the exception and its limits rather than assuming shared access authorizes a combined plan.

clauses.summary: Ensure every text item is readable at the intended plot scale.

questions: Is every text item clear and legible at the intended plotting scale, including dense, rotated and detailed annotations? Review the plotted source, not only the extracted strings.

clauses.summary: Leave a blank 1 cm border margin and crop any excess margin.

questions: Does the border have a1cm white-space margin at intended plotting size? Verify the physical margin rather than using crop-relative PDF coordinates alone.
Have margins exceeding1cm been cropped out while preserving all required plan information?
Is the margin free of information? Inspect every sheet edge and unresolved clipped annotation.

clauses.summary: Identify the plan category in the heading.

questions: Is the applicable plan category identified in the heading using the source Sketch, Surveyor Sketch or Survey designation? Keep hybrid specialization and the separately controlled compiled-plan exemption/heading distinct; a heading text candidate is not professional classification.

clauses.summary: Align the stated plan purpose with the applicable PLAR table purpose and activity.

questions: Has the exact applicable regulator-specific PLAR TableA1/A2 purpose/activity entry and its current edition been independently identified from application evidence? Do not select a row from a disposition code or keyword alone.
Is the purpose wording shown on the plan consistent with that applicable purpose/activity entry? Record discrepancies and unresolved application intent for correction.

clauses.summary: State the complete land description, with applicable theoretic and road-allowance wording.

questions: Does the legal description include the required Within wording? Check the heading against the actual land description.

Where qualified source review establishes that theoretic/theoretical wording applies, does the Within wording include that qualifier? Record the basis; unsurveyed-territory text alone must not silently choose a legal-description interpretation.
Does the legal description identify the applicable Quarter, Section, Township, Range and Meridian completely and accurately? Verify the components against independent cadastral/application records.
Where Lot, Block and Plan apply, are the applicable identifiers included accurately in the legal description?

Where the activity affects road allowances along a section's south or west limits, are those allowances included in that section's legal description as prescribed? Verify the affected allowance/section identities.

Where the activity passes through adjoining theoretic/theoretical road allowances, is the corresponding and-through-adjoining-road-allowances wording included? Record the exact source-backed allowance relationships.

clauses.summary: Match both heading description and illustrated activity extent to the accompanying form.

questions: Is the legal description in the plan heading identical to the legal description on the accompanying application, amendment or renewal form? Missing form evidence remains unresolved.
Do the activity extents illustrated in the body identify the same legal description as the accompanying form? Compare the complete extents rather than matching an isolated legal-description string.

clauses.summary: Give the municipality's full legal name.

questions: Is the municipality's full legal name shown and verified against authoritative municipal/application evidence? Resolve an unclear or absent municipality identity without inventing a name.

clauses.summary: Match the applicant's legal name to both the client registry and the form.

questions: Does the applicant name on the plan match the legal name in the client registry? An operator, consultant or neighbouring-interest label does not independently establish the applicant.
Does that applicant legal name also match the accompanying form? Record absent registry/form evidence separately from a drawing-text candidate.

clauses.summary: The preparing consultant or survey company may be identified.

questions: If the preparer chose to identify the consultant or survey company, is that optional identification clear and correctly associated? Its absence is not a mandatory drawing deficiency.

clauses.summary: Display both a numerical main-plan scale and a graphic scale bar.

questions: Is the numerical main-plan scale shown and correctly associated with the main plan rather than an access map or detail?
Is the graphic scale bar shown for the main plan? Inspect its plotted identity and relationship to the numerical scale; the separate detail-view no-bar provision does not waive the main-plan bar.

clauses.summary: Explain plan symbols and abbreviations in the legend, using standard conventions where practical.

questions: Where qualified review establishes that standard conventions are practicable, are applicable standard symbols and abbreviations used? Consult the relevant current LTO SUR-1 conventions and record any unresolved external-standard or scope issue.
Are the standard symbols and abbreviations actually used explained in the legend? Verify the entire symbol/abbreviation set against the source plan.
Are all other symbols and abbreviations used on the plan explained in the legend? Identify omissions individually and the evidence needed to correct them.

clauses.summary: Keep symbols readable at the intended plot scale.

questions: Are symbols legible at the intended plotting scale, including crowded and detailed locations? Inspect the plotted plan rather than treating symbol-text extraction as proof.

clauses.summary: Include the reference-point symbol and supporting information required for all plan types by the referenced georeferencing guide.

questions: Is the geo-reference point symbol shown in accordance with the applicable Geo-Referencing Guide's all-plan-types requirements? Verify the exact guide edition and source symbol; its presence alone does not verify CRS or coordinate accuracy.
Is the supporting information required by that guide for all plan types shown and internally consistent? Record the guide clauses, plan evidence and any unresolved datum/projection/source questions.

clauses.summary: Indicate main-plan orientation with north arrows.

questions: Inspect the original main plan and verify that north arrow(s) communicate its orientation; request correction where orientation remains unclear.

clauses.summary: Use north-up page orientation unless impractical.

questions: For the documented practical layout, inspect the original sheet and verify north is toward the top; record the layout correction needed.

clauses.summary: Exclude imagery and keep permitted graphic treatments from obscuring data.

questions: Inspect the original plan and verify that it contains no imagery; do not confuse use of imagery as source evidence with permission to embed it.
Inspect any colour, shading, topography or contours against all affected annotations and linework; verify plan data remain readable and identify obscured items.

clauses.summary: Depict the georeferenced point under the cited guide.

questions: Compare the main-plan RP depiction and its tie to the activity with the applicable Geo-Referencing Guide; identify missing source/guide evidence before requesting correction.

clauses.summary: Plot and label cadastral fabric and show full affected quarter sections.

questions: Compare plotted cadastral fabric with independent cadastral/control sources and identify incorrect or unresolved locations.
Compare cadastral labels with authoritative parcel and ATS identities and identify incorrect labels.
Using the established activity extent, verify that every affected quarter section is shown in full; identify clipped or omitted affected quarters.

clauses.summary: Identify government road allowances and their theoretical status.

questions: Inspect government road allowance depiction against cadastral evidence and verify correct labels, including theoretical status where applicable; do not infer road status from graphic proximity.

clauses.summary: Label affected sections and quarter sections.

questions: Compare the entire activity extent with ATS/cadastral evidence and verify that every affected section and/or quarter section is correctly identified in the plan.

clauses.summary: Label LSD or LSD-quarter lines intended as activity limits.

questions: Compare accepted boundary intent with the main plan and verify labels on every LSD or LSD-quarter line intended to define the activity; request missing or incorrect labels.

clauses.summary: Identify unsurveyed territory in the plan body.

questions: For the source-supported unsurveyed territory containing the proposed activity, verify that this status is indicated in the plan body; this annotation does not independently establish ownership.

clauses.summary: Show and confirm specified crossing and nearby land interests.

questions: Using independent land-standing evidence, verify all dispositions through and within 250 m adjacent to the proposed activity are shown; document any empty search result and its source.
Using Land Titles/cadastral evidence, verify all registered boundary surveys through and within 250 m adjacent to the activity are shown.
Using title evidence, verify all titled metes-and-bounds parcels through and within 250 m adjacent to the activity are shown.
Verify applicable titled metes-and-bounds parcels are identified as C. of T.; retain the title-to-parcel association rather than accepting a stray text label.
Compare the depicted interests with the Surface Public Lands Standing Search and record omissions, inconsistent identities or unresolved standing.

clauses.summary: Show applicable hydrography and use the specified fallback source.

questions: Compare the activity and its 100 m adjacent vicinity with independent hydrographic evidence and verify all through/nearby hydrography is shown.
Inspect hydrographic features and verify arrows indicate direction of flow; document any feature-specific applicability uncertainty instead of assuming flow from page linework.
Verify detected unmapped water features relevant to regulation are included; record the detection/source evidence, including support for an assertion that none were detected.
Where surveyed hydrography is unavailable, compare the plan with the 1:20 000 Base Features Hydrography available through AltaLIS and identify missing mapped features.

clauses.summary: Show names for water features where applicable.

questions: For each waterbody or watercourse with an applicable name established from source evidence, verify the correct name is shown and identify needed correction.

clauses.summary: Use an unambiguous bold activity outline without obscuring data.

questions: Compare activity-outline and ordinary line weights on the original plan and verify the outline is 3 to 4 times normal thickness and clearly identifies the activity extent.

Verify the activity outline is solid rather than dashed, subject only to an independently resolved, component-specific source exception; a private-land presentation option must not exempt Crown portions.
Inspect the full activity outline and verify its weight and placement do not obscure plan data; identify affected annotations or linework.

clauses.summary: Exclude the specified road categories from activity extent and area.

questions: Using authoritative road classification, verify surveyed government road allowances (developed or not), registered roads and unregistered public-use roads are excluded from the activity extent.
Compare the area derivation with those classified road exclusions and verify their areas are not included in the activity calculation.

clauses.summary: Include affected theoretical unsurveyed road allowances.

questions: Using authoritative road/cadastral evidence, verify affected theoretical unsurveyed road allowances are included in the activity extent.
Compare the area derivation with the affected theoretical unsurveyed road allowances and verify their areas are included.

clauses.summary: Use straight or constant-radius limits except qualifying natural-bank limits.

questions: Classify every activity-boundary segment from source evidence and verify all portions outside the permanent-natural-bank exception are straight lines or constant-radius arcs.
Review the permitted bank-defined exception only for the identified permanent, naturally occurring water-feature bank portions; do not extend it to artificial, temporary or unresolved features.

clauses.summary: Document and depict the intended qualifying current natural-bank boundary.

questions: Compare available bank evidence and verify the chosen location uses the most accurate information available; preserve source and reading uncertainties.

Where qualified source interpretation confirms that the source sketches permission applies to this plan type and bank evidence, review the option to use the most recent orthorectified aerial or satellite imagery without ground verification. Record that interpretation and professional/regulator limits; do not automatically extend the wording to a Surveyor Sketch, establish source accuracy, or permit imagery on the plan.
Compare the intended activity extent with accepted current-bank evidence and verify the two coincide.
Inspect the activity limit and verify that it follows the current bank sinuosity rather than substituting an unsupported straight or smoothed boundary.
Verify the current bank is depicted by a sinuous line in the original plan.
Verify the current-bank line is not dimensioned; keep independent source observations separate from plotted boundary dimensions.
Inspect the identified natural-bank label and verify it says bank rather than substituting a different water or bank reference.
Verify the plan explains the method used to determine the bank location.
Verify the bank derivation source is identified and linked to the depicted boundary.
Verify the date of the bank derivation source is shown.
On the source-supported titled upland, verify the prior natural boundary on which current title is based is ghosted as a dashed line.
Verify the ghosted prior-title boundary is labelled with the basis used to determine its location.
Verify the bank extends beyond the proposed activity by approximately 30 to 50 m; preserve the source approximation rather than impose an invented exact tolerance.
Verify that extension is shown as a continuous bank line beyond the activity.
Where recent flooding or human alteration makes the current bank unclear, review seeking Alberta Land Surveyor advice; this recommendation is not a missing mandatory plan element.

clauses.summary: Retain optional hectare precision and area-rounding choices.

questions: Review the optional choice to express hectare areas to up to three decimal places; do not turn this permission into a universal precision failure.
If the reviewer establishes the first source range applies, review the optional 0.001 ha precision for areas through 0.999 ha; retain any source-range ambiguity.
If the reviewer establishes the next source range applies, review the optional 0.01 ha precision for areas through 9.99 ha; do not invent an overlapping-band resolution.
For the reviewer-established 10.0 ha-and-above range, review the optional 0.1 ha precision convention.

clauses.summary: Express plan areas in hectares.

questions: Inspect all applicable area annotations and verify hectare units are shown; additional activity-specific units do not remove the hectare requirement.

clauses.summary: Show the entire activity total area.

questions: Compare all activity components and area records with the displayed entire-activity total; resolve conflicting totals and scope mismatches before accepting a candidate value.

clauses.summary: Provide the qualified Timber Damage Assessment breakdown.

questions: Using accepted activity/standing evidence, verify the total-area portion within existing dispositions is stated in the TDA breakdown.
Verify the total-area portion outside existing dispositions is stated in the same TDA breakdown.
Verify this within/outside-existing breakdown is not fragmented by individual land parcel.
Where multiple FMAs are overlapped or activity is partly outside any FMA, verify the within/outside-existing areas are further separated for each overlapped FMA.
For the activity portion outside any FMA, verify its within/outside-existing areas are separately identified in the FMA breakdown.
Verify total incidental-activity area is provided in a separate row of the same breakdown.
For an amendment of an approved disposition, compare the approved record and verify previously approved area is included within existing disposition area to avoid duplicate billing.
Using authoritative status evidence, verify overlapped cancelled-with-outstanding-obligations disposition area is counted outside existing dispositions.

clauses.summary: Label width at every linear-activity width change.

questions: Using the complete accepted linear corridor relationship, inspect each width change and verify its width is labelled; missing source geometry remains manual review.

clauses.summary: State lengths for access-road DLO/LOC and literal PLA activities.

questions: Using the accepted width/length schedule, verify the total length for each distinct width is shown; a LOC code alone does not establish the access-road branch.
Verify the overall activity length is shown and reconciles with the width-based lengths; do not extend the literal PLA route to other pipeline-purpose codes.

clauses.summary: Give each detail a unique identity matching its main-plan reference.

questions: Inspect all detail views and verify every detail has a unique identifier.
Compare each detail identifier/description with its main-plan reference and identify mismatches.

clauses.summary: Label detail scale correctly without requiring a detail scale bar.

questions: Inspect each detail scale or not-to-scale statement and verify it correctly describes that view; retain the scale options under clause1.1.4 rather than impose main-plan ratios.
If a detail scale bar is adopted, review it in context; absence of a detail bar is not a deficiency and does not remove the main title-block bar requirement.

clauses.summary: Keep existing plans consistent between details and the main plan.

questions: Compare existing-plan plotting in each applicable detail with the main body and identify inconsistent locations or extents.
Compare existing-plan labels in each applicable detail with main-body identities and identify inconsistent labels.

clauses.summary: Keep detail symbols and dimensions consistent with the main plan.

questions: Compare each detail symbol with the corresponding main-body symbol and identify inconsistent meaning or depiction.
Compare detail dimensions and their source associations with the main body and identify inconsistent values or endpoints.

clauses.summary: Show linear-activity width in applicable details.

questions: Inspect each applicable linear-activity detail and verify the relevant corridor width is shown, tied to the same feature as the main plan.

clauses.summary: A sketch's reference coordinate may come from one of the listed cadastral, disposition, ATS, control, or existing-survey sources.

questions: If the permitted sketch coordinate-source route is used, identify the actual source: Cadastral Mapping Database, DIDs, ATSv4.1 file coordinates, ASCM or an existing geo-referenced disposition survey plan. Preserve dataset/plan/version and location provenance, and review the separate Geo-Referencing Guide; permission to use a source does not verify its accuracy.

clauses.summary: Dimension sketch extents with metre distances, degree bearings, and corresponding curve elements.

questions: For each non-exempt extent course established by the provenance-backed dimension-scope review, are horizontal distances shown in metres to at least1m precision? Preserve per-course existing-line, natural-bank and applicable Part4 exceptions rather than imposing dimensions on an exempt edge.

Does the private per-course applicability provenance preserve ordinary dimensions on every non-exempt course? A partial exception keeps manual_sketch_extent_dimensions_required true; false is reserved for no ordinary extent-dimension obligations anywhere, and never waives ties.
For those non-exempt extent courses, are full-circle bearings shown to at least1degree precision? Confirm course identity and the scope of any dimension exception.
For every non-exempt boundary curve, is the radius shown to the corresponding distance precision? Preserve full curve identity; graphic Bezier inventory is not cadastral curve evidence.
For every non-exempt boundary curve, is the delta angle shown to the corresponding angular precision? Resolve incomplete or ambiguous curve readings before acceptance.
For every non-exempt boundary curve, is arc length shown to the corresponding distance precision? Verify the source curve relationship without flattening it into a straight edge.

clauses.summary: Show approximate distances and directions between deflections, subject to listed existing-line and terminal exceptions.

questions: Are approximate dimensions shown between all non-exempt deflection points? Use the accepted per-course boundary-role/exception register, including applicable Part4 extent relief, rather than assuming every visible line must be dimensioned.

Does the private per-course applicability provenance preserve ordinary dimensions on every non-exempt course? A partial exception keeps manual_sketch_extent_dimensions_required true; false is reserved for no ordinary extent-dimension obligations anywhere, and never waives ties.

For established section, quarter-section, LSD, LSD-quarter or adjacent approved-disposition boundary segments, is the source permission to omit along-boundary dimensions applied only to those segments? It does not waive sufficient relationship dimensions or independent tie requirements.

Are sufficient dimensions retained to relate the new activity to existing linework after the exact along-extent exceptions are resolved? Identify the required relationships individually; do not use an extent-dimension permission to erase unrelated ties.

Where independently reviewed terminal intent is evident, is the source permission to omit dimensions at linear ends used only for those ends? Preserve endpoint identity and the separate end-tie requirements.

clauses.summary: For a narrow parallel corridor, dimension one edge or its parallel alignment.

questions: For the established access-road/right-of-way corridor with parallel boundaries and width strictly below45.72m (150feet), is one side or its parallel offset/centreline dimensioned consistently? Confirm the applicable width and course scope; equality does not qualify, and partial-boundary permissions must not erase unrelated dimensions or ties.

Does the private per-course applicability provenance preserve ordinary dimensions on every non-exempt course? A partial exception keeps manual_sketch_extent_dimensions_required true; false is reserved for no ordinary extent-dimension obligations anywhere, and never waives ties.

clauses.summary: Make deflection and terminal points clear, adding symbols or leaders where needed.

questions: Are each deflection and terminal point apparent and correctly associated with the activity boundary? Review endpoint/feature identities rather than page proximity alone.
Where qualified review finds the points unclear, are X symbols, arrows or leaders used to make deflection and terminal positions clear? Verify their actual association with the intended point.

clauses.summary: Tie each end of the disposition to the nearest ATS corner or a definable point on an existing plan.

questions: For a linear disposition, is each end tied to its nearest ATS corner or a definable point on an existing plan? Verify both endpoint identities, source plan/control provenance and each tie separately.

Where qualified interpretation establishes how the source's both-ends requirement applies to a non-linear disposition, are the interpreted ends tied to the nearest ATS corner or a definable point on an existing plan? Retain that interpretation and source locators; do not invent opposite ends.

clauses.summary: Provide at least two suitable ties for every separate segment.

questions: For every separate non-contiguous segment, are at least two ties shown? Verify the count per segment, not merely two ties for the whole plan; this requirement does not authorize otherwise prohibited non-contiguity.
Do those ties connect to ATS corners or definable points on existing plans with independently resolved endpoint/feature identities and source provenance?

If ties between segments are used under the source permission, are their endpoints and relationship to the required per-segment tie network explicit? The permission does not waive minimum tie coverage or grant plan-combination approval.

clauses.summary: Certify a Surveyor Sketch with the prescribed public-lands declaration, signatures, and matching date.

questions: Is the Surveyor Sketch certified using the applicable Alberta Land Surveyor's Statutory Declaration for Public Lands Dispositions from the Public Lands Survey Manual? Verify that external source's exact version, form and applicability.
Is the declaration signed by a licensed Alberta Land Surveyor, with the professional identity/authorization independently confirmed?
Is the declaration date consistent with the version date of this plan? Resolve mismatched revisions or missing dates.
Is the declaration signed by a Commissioner for Oaths as required for this source branch? Review the actual declaration/signature evidence rather than a text mention.

clauses.summary: Include the additional survey-plan information specified by the referenced georeferencing guide.

questions: Identify the applicable Geo-Referencing Guide edition and its additional Plan Requirements for Survey Plans. Inspect the title block, legend and notes for the required information, retaining exact guide citations; this manual does not itself reproduce those external requirements.

clauses.summary: Certify the survey plan with the prescribed public-lands declaration, required signatures, and matching date.

questions: Inspect the applicable Alberta Land Surveyor statutory declaration for Public Lands Dispositions and record the Public Lands Survey Manual edition/form used. Compiled plans take the separate Appendix D replacement route under 3.6.1.3.
Inspect the Alberta Land Surveyor signature and independently confirm the signer is licensed; a typed name or text occurrence is not signature or licence verification.
Compare the declaration date with the plan version date and resolve inconsistencies using the original signed document.

Inspect the Commissioner for Oaths signature required by the ordinary declaration route. Do not carry this ordinary-route requirement into the compiled Appendix D replacement without checking that form.

clauses.summary: Relate the disposition's location to known survey evidence.

questions: Show and independently verify how the disposition is located relative to known survey evidence. Retain evidence identities and source/control relationships rather than accepting proximity of PDF strokes.

clauses.summary: Apply the monument types specified by the applicable PLAR table.

questions: Identify the exact applicable PLAR table row and its monument alternatives, then compare the monuments placed with that row. Do not select monument requirements from the disposition code alone or treat a text mention as placement evidence.

clauses.summary: Use non-monumented or computed point categories only where their purpose is clear, recognizing the stated discouragement.

questions: Where discouraged temporary/calculated/computed/non-monumented points are used and the applicable PLAR row does not allow no monument, is their intent clear? Record the professional rationale; the source discourages these categories rather than imposing an absolute ban.
Where the applicable PLAR entry allows no monument, document that limited exception and its conditions. Do not infer an exemption from unrelated evidence or hybrid-point requirements.

clauses.summary: Show the evidence supporting relationships with all affected dispositions and other interests.

questions: Inspect all evidence used to establish the disposition boundary relationships with affected dispositions and other interests. Retain the underlying records, tie identities and unresolved conflicts.

clauses.summary: For access roads, identify shared boundaries or parallel overlaps and show common-evidence ties supporting them.

questions: Identify and clearly depict every common boundary or parallel overlap with other dispositions, using the authoritative source plans.
Show ties to common evidence for both disposition plans supporting each common-boundary or parallel-offset determination; retain source and independent verification records.

clauses.summary: Dimension survey boundaries at the stated LTO distance, bearing, and curve precision.

questions: Inspect every boundary horizontal distance for metre units and stated precision to 0.01m under the referenced LTO standard; coordinate precision is not proof of positional accuracy.
Inspect full-circle boundary bearings for the stated precision of 5 arc seconds, retaining the source bearing basis and applicable LTO reference.

For each boundary curve, inspect radius, delta angle and arc length at the corresponding precision. Preserve actual curve definitions in specialist CAD artifacts; do not replace them with graphic Bezier inventory or a flattened straight ring.

clauses.summary: Dimension the ends of linear activities except square terminations.

questions: Identify each non-square termination and inspect its end dimensions. The exception applies to ends at 90 degrees to the boundary; verify it per end rather than waiving all terminal information.

clauses.summary: Identify acquisition date and source for remotely sensed access-road survey data.

questions: Identify the remotely sensed survey-data source on the plan and retain the underlying dataset/source identity.
Identify the remotely sensed data acquisition date on the plan; do not substitute PDF creation time or report generation time.

clauses.summary: Follow the referenced natural-boundary submission rules and tabulate verification and direct-observation coordinates.

questions: Identify and review the applicable Plan Requirements in the Directive on updated plan submissions for changes in natural boundaries; retain edition, applicability and exact references.
Inspect natural-boundary depiction against the applicable LTO SUR-1 requirements, separately from this manual citation.
Inspect the tabulated coordinates of ground-verification points with their source and evidence roles; PDF page points do not qualify.
Inspect the tabulated coordinates of direct bank observations and their independent provenance/control. Do not invent accepted boundary coordinates from nearby annotation.

clauses.summary: For a qualifying large lease amendment, the existing-boundary survey may be limited and the itemized area must be clearly shown.

questions: For the qualifying existing lease of at least 10ha, review the limited survey of existing boundaries adjacent to the amendment and its itemized-plan treatment. Confirm that the threshold uses the existing lease area, not only the changed area.
Inspect the entire amended-area boundary in bold, including the boundary common with the existing area.
Verify the existing and amended areas are clearly and distinctly labelled using the authoritative amendment record.

clauses.summary: Show improvements and buried infrastructure that affect amended lease boundaries.

questions: Show and identify surface improvements affecting the amended disposition boundaries; verify their relationship independently.
Show and identify buried facilities affecting the amended disposition boundaries, retaining the source and unresolved location limits.

clauses.summary: A long linear disposition with a limited amendment may use an itemized survey of only adjacent existing boundaries.

questions: Review itemized treatment limiting the existing-boundary survey to boundaries adjacent to the amendment. The literal source branch is total length greater than 6.5km and at most two affected quarters; exactly 6.5km requires separately recorded direction.
Inspect the entire amended-area boundary in bold, including its common boundary with the existing area.
Confirm existing and amended areas are clearly and separately labelled on the itemized presentation.

clauses.summary: Retrace a shorter surveyed linear disposition in full where its boundary still applies.

questions: Review full retracement of the existing disposition where it continues to define the boundary. Identify any portions that no longer define it and retain their source-backed exception; exactly 6.5km is not silently treated as less than 6.5km.

clauses.summary: Retrace the entire disposition when an amendment affects more than two quarter sections.

questions: Review retracement of the entire disposition when the amendment affects more than two quarter sections. This source condition does not depend on the total-length comparison.

clauses.summary: For an itemized addition/deletion, identify changed land, areas, key map, and the complete amended digital polygon.

questions: Inspect the title block for a clear statement that the survey adds and/or deletes land from the disposition.
Compare the legal description with only the land being added/deleted; do not silently substitute the whole unchanged disposition description.
Inspect the added/deleted land illustration in the main plan body, distinguishing each change.
Colour may illustrate the added/deleted land; lack of colour alone is not a deficiency.
Inspect the stated added/deleted area and the total/remaining area, preserving which figure describes which land.
Inspect a key map showing the added/deleted portion and the total/remaining disposition.
Inspect the actual PCS/OneStop DWG or shape polygon for the entire disposition as amended, not only the changed portion. No consistency check is executed without those artifacts.
When both adding and deleting land on one itemized plan, verify both change classes are separately shown with the required descriptions, illustrations and areas.

The cited source states that survey plans cannot be amended with itemized sketches. Review the proposed itemized-sketch route against the independently classified existing survey plan on file, retaining both classification and presentation evidence. This is a manual conflict question, not an automated FAIL, eligibility determination or inference from a title/length.

clauses.summary: Use legend-defined unmonumented-point symbols for accepted hybrid coordinates on a conventional plan.

questions: Inspect the conventional plan for accepted XC/RC points shown with legend-defined unmonumented-point symbols.
Confirm hybrid coordinate symbols are not carried into the conventional plan as the accepted-point symbols; inspect the actual legend and drawing.

clauses.summary: Identify an accepted XC with its source point, plan, disposition, and version.

questions: For each accepted XC, inspect the original hybrid-plan point number. The source does not prescribe identifier order.
For each accepted XC, inspect the source plan number and retain its exact source snapshot.
For each accepted XC, inspect the source disposition number without rewriting the disposition identity.
For each accepted XC, inspect the source plan version date and compare it with the accepted source record.

clauses.summary: Mark an accepted RC as accepted and provide the same source identifiers used for accepted XCs.

questions: Inspect every accepted RC for an accepted label.
For each accepted RC, inspect the original hybrid-plan point number using the accepted-XC information format.
For each accepted RC, inspect the source plan number using the accepted-XC information format.
For each accepted RC, inspect the source disposition number using the accepted-XC information format.
For each accepted RC, inspect the source version date using the accepted-XC information format; identifier order is not prescribed.

clauses.summary: Use the applicable PLAR table monumentation for the conventional plan.

questions: Compare the conventional-plan monumentation with the exact applicable PLAR Table A1/A2 row and its conditions. Existing-hybrid interaction does not itself establish monument requirements.

clauses.summary: Identify the survey as hybrid in its heading.

questions: Inspect the main heading for the prescribed hybrid-survey wording and its stated purpose. A whole-span heading candidate does not independently establish legal plan classification.

clauses.summary: Include the prescribed hybrid statements about governing coordinates, reference system/derivation, ground units, and scale factor.

questions: Inspect the statement that the plan contains governing coordinates; verify its intended legal/evidence role independently.
Inspect the coordinate/bearing reference statement for the applicable UTM zone, NAD83(CSRS), Epoch 2002 and stated GNSS derivation method. Text presence does not verify the actual CRS or control.
Inspect the statement identifying distances as ground metres and decimals thereof, and compare it with the actual measurement basis.
Inspect the stated combined scale factor to six decimal places and retain the source/basis used; do not derive a verified transformation from a displayed number alone.

clauses.summary: Applicable standard hybrid coordinate abbreviations and symbols may be added to the standard legend.

questions: If applicable hybrid coordinate abbreviations/symbols are added to the standard legend, compare the chosen EC/XC/RC/OC entries with the cited standard conventions. This optional clause does not require every category to exist on every plan; coordinate-table type fields are addressed separately.

clauses.summary: Number the coordinate table sequentially from one without gaps or inserted suffix numbers.

questions: Inspect the coordinate-table point numbering sequence for a start at 1.
Inspect the entire sequence for missing numbers or inserted suffix/decimal numbers; retain the complete source-linked table rather than an incomplete extracted sample.

clauses.summary: Format table northings/eastings to two decimals without grouping spaces or commas.

questions: Inspect original formatted northings and eastings for two decimal places; floating-point serialization alone does not establish the displayed precision.
Inspect coordinate strings for absence of grouping spaces and commas. Preserve original strings and source provenance when checking formatting.

clauses.summary: Identify each tabulated coordinate's EC, XC, RC, or OC category.

questions: Inspect every table row for the applicable EC, XC, RC or OC category and verify its evidence role. Category text alone does not establish acceptance or governing status.

clauses.summary: Describe each coordinate accurately and identify applicable point attributes.

questions: Inspect each point description for accuracy and consistency with the plan; do not impose a wording template where the source leaves the description open.
Inspect applicable RP, PC and CC attributes in the point descriptions and compare their actual roles with the table and drawing.

clauses.summary: For existing establishment coordinates, preserve source coordinates and identify their provenance under the new plan numbering.

questions: Inspect XC point numbers in the new plan sequence, retaining the mapping to their original source point identities.
Compare each XC northing/easting with the exact source values from the creating plan; do not round or recompute them to force agreement.

For each XC inspect the required provenance identifiers: original point, source plan, disposition and version date, in any order. For an unfiled source, review the expressly permitted job/revision alternative per record rather than demanding absent filed-plan identifiers or waiving identifiers for all other XCs.
For an unfiled source plan, review the permitted use of the plan job number and revision number in place of the stated source identifiers, retaining the unfiled source snapshot and mapping.

clauses.summary: Enclose body-of-plan point numbers in ellipses.

questions: Inspect body-of-plan point numbers for the prescribed ellipse enclosure; plain text extraction cannot verify this graphical condition.

clauses.summary: Order hybrid point numbers logically from reference points through new boundaries and then other locations.

questions: Inspect point-number order beginning with the geo-referenced point or points.
Inspect incremental numbering along the new boundary in a logical sequence.
Inspect remaining point numbers at other locations for a logical subsequent sequence and correspondence with the coordinate table.

clauses.summary: Natural-boundary OC labels may be thinned on the plan body to avoid clutter while retaining selected table references.

questions: Review any thinning of natural-boundary OC labels in the plan body to avoid clutter: selected point numbers at regular intervals may be used. This is not permission to omit necessary coordinates from the table.

clauses.summary: Exclude calculated and temporary points from hybrid plans.

questions: Inspect the hybrid plan for exclusion of calculated points; do not treat a closing calculation as an accepted governing coordinate.
Inspect the hybrid plan for exclusion of temporary points, separately from evidence/control used during reconstruction.

clauses.summary: Tabulate curve-end OC/RC identifiers, coordinates, categories, and descriptions for existing curves.

questions: Inspect table point numbers and northings/eastings for OC and/or RC points at the beginning and end of each existing curve used.
Inspect the endpoint coordinate categories and descriptions, preserving their accepted source identities and relationships to the existing curve.

clauses.summary: Label point numbers and type symbols for points on the existing curve portions used.

questions: Inspect body labels for the point number and coordinate-type symbol of every point on each existing curve or curve portion actually used; reconcile table and drawing completeness.

clauses.summary: Dimension existing curves with radius, delta, and arc length.

questions: Inspect the radius for each existing curve used.
Inspect the delta angle for each existing curve used.
Inspect the arc length for each existing curve used, preserving the source curve rather than flattening it for straight-ring QA.

clauses.summary: Tabulate point identifiers, coordinates, categories, and descriptions for all points on new curves.

questions: Inspect coordinate-table point numbers and northings/eastings for all points on every new hybrid curve.
Inspect coordinate categories and descriptions for all points on new curves, retaining source/derived identity and accepted roles.

clauses.summary: Assign PC/CC attributes to exactly the three curve-defining points in the table descriptions.

questions: Identify the three curve-defining points and inspect PC and/or CC attributes in their table descriptions; exactly those three defining points receive the curve-defining attributes.
Placing PC/CC at the start of the description is preferred by the source, not mandatory; do not create a deficiency merely from a different position.

clauses.summary: Label the three defining points of every new curve with point number and coordinate-type symbol.

questions: Inspect the plan body for the point number and coordinate-type symbol of the three defining points of each new curve, matching the table and accepted curve definition.

clauses.summary: Dimension new hybrid curves with radius, delta, and arc length.

questions: Inspect the radius of each new hybrid curve.
Inspect the delta angle of each new hybrid curve.
Inspect the arc length of each new hybrid curve; no curve calculation or acceptance is performed by this manual-question path.

clauses.summary: Show at least one mapping reference point using an allowed physical monument.

questions: Inspect at least one mapping reference point on the hybrid plan and retain its source/evidence identity.
Confirm the RP is an allowed found/placed statutory iron post, standard post, found iron bar or appropriate ASCM. A symbol or flag alone does not independently establish the monument or control.

clauses.summary: Show at least two observed coordinates on the hybrid plan.

questions: Inspect at least two observed coordinates on the plan, verifying OC roles and complete source-linked records rather than counting arbitrary coordinate strings.

clauses.summary: Keep every establishment, existing-establishment, and re-establishment coordinate within 10 km of an observed coordinate.

questions: For every EC, XC and RC, review distance to an OC and the inclusive 10km limit using complete accepted roles, independently verified metric CRS/provenance and the full OC set. No numerical or spatial-acceptance result is asserted by this workbook.

clauses.summary: Apply the explicit compiled-plan exemptions before selecting heading, monumentation, or amendment checks.

questions: Confirm the compiled-plan exemption from the ordinary heading clause 1.2.1.1, all monumentation clauses in 3.2.1, and all amendment clauses in 3.3. Retain all other applicable general/survey content and the separate declaration replacement in 3.6.1.3.

clauses.summary: Use a heading identifying compilation from existing surveys and its purpose.

questions: Inspect the main heading identifying compilation from existing surveys and its purpose, using the prescribed compiled-plan wording. Compare the purpose with the application; a heading candidate is not verified plan classification.

clauses.summary: Have an Alberta Land Surveyor sign the Appendix D compiled-plan declaration in place of the ordinary survey declaration.

questions: Inspect the statutory declaration in Appendix D of the applicable Public Lands Survey Manual used for the compiled plan; this replaces the ordinary section 3.1.2 declaration route.

Inspect the Alberta Land Surveyor signature for the compiled Appendix D declaration and independently review the current form requirements. Do not import a Commissioner-for-Oaths obligation from the replaced ordinary declaration without authority.

clauses.summary: Show no new monuments or new fieldwork on a compiled plan.

questions: Inspect the compiled plan for absence of newly placed monuments; distinguish new work from permitted depiction of existing evidence.
Inspect the compiled-plan presentation and source records for absence of new fieldwork. This is not permission to invent control or provenance.

clauses.summary: Explain retained astronomic bearings or identify grid rotations, as applicable.

questions: Where astronomic bearings are retained, inspect an appropriate bearing statement.
Where astronomic bearings are retained, inspect the corresponding grid bearing in the legend.
Where bearings are grid and source plans were rotated, inspect the stated rotation angle for every rotated source plan, retaining source identities and accepted rotations.

clauses.summary: Use legend-defined annotations for compiled dimensions and rotated bearings.

questions: Inspect compiled dimensions for a legend-defined annotation symbol and reconcile each annotated source dimension with its source plan.
Inspect all rotated bearings for their legend-defined annotation symbol and compare with the actual source rotation records.

clauses.summary: Make symbol and annotation usage agree with legend classifications of source dimensions, fixed/calculated values, rotations, and new unmonumented corners.

questions: Compare legend classifications with dimensions taken from the primary source plan and every other source plan.
Compare legend classifications with fixed dimensions on the compiled plan.
Compare legend classifications with calculated dimensions, retaining their provenance and role.
Compare legend classifications with rotated bearings and their source rotations.
Compare legend classifications with new unmonumented corners. This classification does not authorize new monuments or new fieldwork on a compiled plan.

clauses.summary: Depict existing monuments with standard found-evidence symbols and identify that legend class as existing evidence.

questions: Inspect existing monuments for standard found-evidence symbols.
Inspect the corresponding legend class labelled as existing evidence; do not present it as newly found/placed work without source support.

clauses.summary: Avoid transcribing source-plan monument descriptions; limit any description to applicable ATS location.

questions: Inspect the compiled plan for source-plan monument descriptions copied beyond the source allowance.

Limit any applicable monument description to identifying the ATS location of the evidence; retain fuller source descriptions in the evidence register rather than transcribing them as new plan evidence.

clauses.summary: Use the specified application/plan route when adding land to an existing EZE/REA.

questions: Record the source-backed interpretation or regulator direction for the three listed EZE/REA addition routes. Do not automatically require all three cumulatively or invent a single exclusive route.
Review the listed new EZE/REA activity-number route if adopted, retaining the relationship to the existing disposition.
Review the listed itemized plan associated with the existing plan if adopted, retaining the exact source plan and changed-land identity.
Review the listed whole-EZE/REA amendment route if adopted. An application lifecycle labelled initial does not by itself disqualify an addition pursued under a new number.

clauses.summary: Show a VCE continuously or using the permitted separate-shape sketch presentation.

questions: Review the permitted continuous-linear VCE presentation; the source does not require every permitted presentation simultaneously.

Review the permitted non-contiguous multi-shape sketch presentation for the VCE. The clause literally names VCE and sketch; it does not automatically extend this permission to RVC or every survey subtype.

clauses.summary: Choose an allowed presentation for a linear activity spanning public and non-public land.

questions: Identify which of the three source-listed mixed-land presentations is used and confirm its scope. Do not interpret the alternatives as three cumulative drawing requirements.
Review presentation as non-contiguous public-land segments, without treating the private-land gap as acquired Crown geometry.
For the public-segments alternative, inspect that those segments are on the same sheet.
For the public-segments alternative, inspect the one-township condition; do not apply it indiscriminately to the other alternatives.
Review the continuous presentation with dashed outline over private land, preserving land/feature identity.
Review the continuous presentation with a bold outline for the entire public/private activity; its additional heading and parcel labels are addressed by4.1.1.5.

clauses.summary: Describe only the public-land segments in the heading when using either segmented public-land or dashed private-land presentation.

questions: Inspect the heading legal descriptions for only the public-land segments when using the segmented-public or dashed-private alternative. Compare with the actual parcel/land components.

clauses.summary: Describe all parcels and label their Crown/Freehold status when bold outlining the entire mixed-land activity.

questions: Inspect legal descriptions for all parcels in the heading when bold-outlining the entire mixed-land activity.
Inspect each parcel for its Crown or Freehold label within the parcel. These are drawing-context labels, not independent title verification or a claim that the private portion is Crown-owned.

clauses.summary: Secure prior regulator approval for a long continuous linear plan that cannot meet sheet-size limits.

questions: Inspect prior regulator approval for the continuous long-linear presentation that cannot meet sheet-size limits, identifying the exact activity and approval scope. This is not a blanket multipage or size waiver.

clauses.summary: Limit a multi-polygon piezometer/heave-monument application and its access to a six-mile-square extent unless excepted.

questions: Review the entire multi-site application extent against the stated six-mile-by-six-mile limit. It is a spatial extent, not an equivalent hectare/acre cap.
Where a regulator exception applies, inspect its exact application, extent and conditions; do not infer it from plan size or nearby unrelated approvals.

Consider consequences of future amendments across many sites: a change to one site may require retracement of the entire survey. The advisory may wording does not itself impose automatic full retracement.

clauses.summary: Use a general permitted scale or one of the extra scales allowed for non-peat exploration.

questions: Inspect the chosen scale against the general permitted scales or the extra non-peat SME/RME scales 1:20000, 1:25000 and 1:30000, retaining any applicable source-backed exception.

clauses.summary: Keep the applicant's new SME application outside the stated separation from its existing SME applications.

questions: Review separation of the new SME from the same applicant existing SME applications. The source writes six miles (9.6km); retain the controlling interpretation and search evidence rather than inventing an exact conversion or near-edge acceptance. This clause does not automatically cover RME.

clauses.summary: Use a separate SME/RME number for each contiguous non-peat activity.

questions: Inspect one SME/RME number per contiguous non-peat activity. If a surveyed road allowance or registered road splits the activity, review the source-backed exception and retain the affected segments rather than automatically splitting or combining them.

clauses.summary: Keep non-peat exploration within the stated acreage limit and tabulate exclusions where used.

questions: Review the stated non-peat SME/RME activity area against the 320-acre maximum using the authoritative extent and source units; do not infer a verified area from a PDF text label.
When exclusions are used, inspect a table of gross activity-extent area in both hectares and acres.
When exclusions are used, inspect the exclusions and their acreages, with total excluded area in both hectares and acres.
When exclusions are used, inspect net area (gross extent less exclusions) in both hectares and acres. This specific table is not waived by the general hectare-only presentation rule.

clauses.summary: The non-peat exploration area need not use the general timber-assessment breakdown.

questions: Confirm the non-peat SME/RME exception to the forestry/timber-assessment breakdown in1.3.6.4 only. Other total-area and activity-specific area-reporting requirements remain.

clauses.summary: Show and label every existing disposition inside the proposed non-peat exploration area.

questions: Inspect every existing disposition within the proposed non-peat SME/RME area for depiction and labelling, using the applicable current search and source records. This does not silently reduce the separate general nearby-interest requirements.

clauses.summary: Mark proposed test holes with a legend-defined symbol.

questions: Inspect proposed test-hole locations for TH, X or another suitable explained symbol; do not require one literal symbol where the source permits alternatives.
Inspect the legend for identification of the test-hole symbol actually used.

clauses.summary: Draw dashed access routes to each proposed test hole.

questions: Inspect dashed access routes to every proposed test hole, reconciling all holes and access connections against the actual activity evidence.

clauses.summary: Show all watercourse crossings for the non-peat exploration activity.

questions: Inspect all watercourse crossings of the non-peat exploration activity for depiction and reconcile completeness with the authoritative activity/watercourse evidence.

clauses.summary: Contours may be included on a non-peat exploration plan.

questions: Contours may be included for non-peat exploration; lack of contours is not a deficiency under this clause. The reference to available AltaLIS Base Features data does not make inclusion mandatory.

clauses.summary: Use an allowed peat-exploration scale and add details or labels if the smaller presentation obscures extent.

questions: Inspect the peat exploration/extraction scale against the general scales or 1:20000, 1:25000 and 1:30000, or the source conditional smaller-scale option. A ratio candidate alone does not establish clear intent.
Review the option up to1:40000 only while the intent of the extent is clear; do not treat a smaller scale as unconditionally permitted.
Where extent intent is unclear, inspect sufficient detail views and/or labels to make it clear; do not demand both alternatives where the source permits either.

clauses.summary: Show and label specified interests directly affecting the peat-exploration extent.

questions: Inspect depiction and labels for dispositions directly affecting the peat-activity extent.
Inspect depiction and labels for titled metes-and-bounds parcels directly affecting the peat-activity extent.
Inspect depiction and labels for LTO-registered boundary surveys directly affecting the peat-activity extent; no unstated exemption from the general nearby-interest search/display rule is inferred.

clauses.summary: The peat-exploration area need not use the general timber-assessment breakdown.

questions: Confirm the peat-related SME/RME exception to the forestry/timber-assessment breakdown in1.3.6.4 only. Retain other applicable area requirements.

clauses.summary: Use one disposition number for each contiguous non-peat material activity in this branch.

questions: Inspect one disposition number per contiguous non-peat material activity in this branch. Review any surveyed-road-allowance/registered-road split exception using its actual source and affected components; do not assume every road creates an exception.

clauses.summary: Keep the applicant's new SML application outside the stated separation from its existing SML applications.

questions: Review the new SML separation from the same applicant existing SML applications. Preserve the source six-miles (9.6km) wording and resolve its unit interpretation near the boundary. Do not extend this literal SML clause to all RML/SMC/RMC/DMS applications.

clauses.summary: Show contours for the surface-material activities in the specified non-peat branch.

questions: Inspect contours for the specified non-peat material branch. The source names available AltaLIS Base Features data; unlike4.3.1.10, contour inclusion here is required by the cited edition.

clauses.summary: Limit the overlapping surface-material lease to one SML/RML activity per MSL activity.

questions: Inspect that only one SML/RML activity is associated with each related oil-sands MSL activity, using authoritative application/disposition records.

clauses.summary: Match the overlapping SML/RML boundary to its related approved MSL boundary.

questions: Compare the overlapping SML/RML activity boundary with the related approved MSL boundary, retaining the approved source plan and accepted feature identity. No geometric match is asserted without the actual artifacts.

clauses.summary: For a qualifying final sketch, use the surveyed MSL boundary and identify its source instead of extent dimensions.

questions: Inspect the related MSL survey and its approved/source status; this final-sketch branch requires the related MSL to be surveyed.

Review the conditional relief from dimensions along qualifying coincident activity extents. It does not waive independent ties or relationship dimensions. A partial-course exception must not set the whole-subject manual_sketch_extent_dimensions_required fact false: keep that fact true if any ordinary extent-dimension question applies and retain a private per-course exception/non-exempt register.
Inspect MSL-number labels throughout the coincident activity extents, matching the related approved disposition.
Inspect source plan-number labels throughout the coincident activity extents, matching the surveyed MSL source.
Inspect source version-date labels throughout the coincident activity extents and resolve source-version conflicts.
Inspect scale up to1:20000 or an applicable regulator-granted exception, retaining its exact scope. Do not apply this final-plan relief to an application-stage sketch or unrelated material activity.

clauses.summary: Use one disposition number per contiguous peat-related activity in the listed material-disposition family.

questions: Inspect one disposition number per contiguous peat-related material activity. Review any source-backed surveyed-road-allowance/registered-road split exception without inferring a general non-contiguity permission.

clauses.summary: Keep a peat-related SML within 500 hectares.

questions: Review the peat-related SML area against the stated maximum500ha using independently sourced extent/area evidence. The literal SML limit is not automatically a limit for RML, SMC/RMC or DMS.

clauses.summary: Show the existing bank, applicable full-supply level, and their determination methods.

questions: Inspect the existing bank depiction, retaining the actual bank/subject feature identity.
Inspect the bank-determination method stated on the plan and its imagery plus site-inspection basis; source/observation dates and methods are not proved by a plotted line alone.
Where applicable, inspect the Full Supply Level depiction and its relationship to the activity extent.
Where applicable, inspect the method stated for determining Full Supply Level and retain its supporting evidence.

clauses.summary: Place the freehold-land portion of the activity extent at the bank.

questions: Inspect the freehold activity extent at the bank under the cited rule. Preserve its private/freehold identity within the Crown-submission context; this does not establish Crown ownership or certify title.

clauses.summary: Place the public-land portion of the activity extent at full-supply level unless an applicable exception is established.

questions: Where the public-land FSL rule applies, inspect the activity extent at Full Supply Level and retain the determination evidence.

Where an exception is claimed, inspect its exact authoritative/regulator basis and the resulting activity-extent treatment. The source mentions exceptions but does not list them; do not invent a blanket waiver.

clauses.summary: Show and label adjacent freehold land.

questions: Inspect adjacent freehold lands for depiction and FRH/freehold labelling, retaining the cadastral/source evidence and unresolved ownership questions.

clauses.summary: Identify inlet and water-control works and apply for them as separate activities.

questions: Inspect identification of each inlet on the plan.
Inspect identification of each water-control device on the plan.
Inspect separate activity applications for the inlet and water-control works that are present; do not treat their depiction alone as a filed/approved application.
The separate inlet/control activities may overlap this DLO/LOC. Review the permitted overlap without treating it as a requirement that overlap must occur.

clauses.summary: Identify the public-land-sale purpose in the title block.

questions: Inspect the public-land-sale purpose stated in the title block, comparing it with the application. The source example sketch heading does not independently decide every PLS plan-type requirement.

clauses.summary: Select the analogous Table A1 activity for a DRS and restrict its use to Alberta government ministries.

questions: Inspect the applicant identity and authority against the restriction of DRS use to ministries of the Government of Alberta; do not infer eligibility from a DRS code alone.
Identify the comparable non-DRS PLAR TableA1 activity and its purpose using authoritative application evidence; retain the exact row/mapping and any unresolved regulator differences.

Review the requirements for that comparable non-DRS activity subject to the stated DRS exceptions, retaining DRS as the actual disposition identity. No external TableA1 rule set is imported automatically by this workbook.

clauses.summary: Accept a sketch for specified Transportation and Economic Corridors DRS operations, subject to risk-based survey escalation.

questions: Review the narrow TEC pit/stockpile/haul-road sketch permission in its actual application context, retaining current regulator direction rather than claiming department approval.

Where risk review supports the sketch route, review its sufficiency for consideration or department approval. The permission is not a blanket rule for every DRS applicant, purpose or surveyor-sketch subtype.

Where specific risks warrant escalation, review whether a survey plan is required and retain the regulator/professional direction, including conflicts with other dispositions. Unknown risk must not default to low risk.
